sections.h2: Where is Charleston and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Charleston sits on Charleston Harbor, where the Ashley, Cooper and Wando rivers meet, just south of the middle of South Carolina's coastline. It is the state's most populous city and the seat of Charleston County.

The city covers 135.51 square miles, of which 115.03 is land and 20.48 is water. It reaches into two counties, Charleston and Berkeley, which matters for a seller because the county decides which assessor and treasurer you deal with.

Wikipedia describes six city districts: Downtown (the peninsula between the Ashley and Cooper), West Ashley, Johns Island, James Island, the Cainhoy Peninsula and Daniel Island. A peninsula house and a Johns Island house can sit in the same city but face different flood exposure, parking rules and rental rules.

sections.h2: What is the short history of Charleston?
sections.html:
English colonists founded the settlement as Charles Town in 1670 at Albemarle Point and moved it to its present site in 1680. The city was incorporated on August 13, 1783, and the spelling "Charleston" soon became standard.

The Civil War began in Charleston Harbor with the shelling of Fort Sumter in 1861.

sections.h2: How big is Charleston and what drives its economy?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 150,227 residents, up from 120,083 in 2010 and 96,650 in 2000. The 2025 estimate is 159,423, and the three-county metro area (Charleston, Berkeley and Dorchester) had 849,417 people in 2020.

Wikipedia lists tourism, the port, logistics, aerospace and information technology as the economic base. The Port of Charleston is one of the busiest in the country, Boeing has an aerospace presence, and the tech sector has earned the nickname "Silicon Harbor." The College of Charleston and The Citadel are the two colleges named for the city.

sections.h2: What does Charleston's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
The climate is humid subtropical, with mild winters, hot humid summers and rain all year. Average annual precipitation is about 52.5 inches at the airport and 44.3 inches downtown, and nearly half of it falls from June through September.

Hurricanes are the big risk. Hurricane Hugo, a Category 4 storm, struck on September 21, 1989, and caused more than $2.8 billion in damage. Storm history is worth gathering before you list: repair records, roof age and any past water damage.

  • Average relative humidity at the airport is 72.7%.
  • The record airport high is 105 degrees Fahrenheit (August 1, 1999) and the record low is 6 degrees (January 21, 1985).
  • Rain falls in every season, with summer the wettest.

sections.h2: How does flooding affect selling a house in Charleston?
sections.html:
Flooding is a routine part of the sale conversation in Charleston, because the city sits at about 3 feet of elevation. The city's floodplain page lists the Stono, Ashley, Cooper and Wando rivers, several creeks and the Atlantic Ocean as flood sources.

The same page says a property outside the FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area can still have local drainage trouble, unmapped floodplain or sea level rise. The city issues a Flood Hazard Information Letter that shows a property's flood zone, and elevation certificates and flood hazard information can be requested from floodplain-info@charleston-sc.gov. Its 2019 Flooding and Sea Level Rise Strategy recommends planning for 2.0 to 3.0 feet of sea level rise over the next 50 years.

An owner who thinks the FEMA map is wrong can file a Letter of Map Change with FEMA, for example when the lot sits above the Base Flood Elevation or has been filled. Read more on the city's Floodplain Mapping page. The page notes that an elevation certificate sent with a map request can be flagged for compliance problems such as inadequate flood openings in a garage enclosure.

sections.h2: Who bills Charleston property tax and when is it due?
sections.html:
The Charleston County Assessor values the property and the Charleston County Treasurer bills and collects it. Real estate tax is due January 15 of the following year without penalty.

The Treasurer's page sets the late schedule: 3% after January 15, another 7% after February 1 (10% total), and another 5% after March 17 (15% total). After March 17 the bill goes to the Delinquent Tax Department. State law backs this schedule, and a U.S. postmark decides whether a mailed payment was on time (S.C. Code 12-45-180).

The Treasurer does not accept partial payments, because state law does not allow them. Online payment carries a surcharge. The office is at 101 Meeting St., Suite 120, Charleston, SC 29401, and the phone is (843) 958-4360. The page does not describe how taxes are handled at a closing, so ask the Treasurer or your title company.

sections.h2: How does the Charleston County reassessment work?
sections.html:
South Carolina reassesses every five years, and Charleston County's most recent notices were mailed August 20, 2025. The Assessor says it appraises about 190,000 real property parcels and 6,500 titled mobile homes.

When market value rises more than 15%, the taxable value increase is capped at 15% over the prior value. The page adds that the cap does not limit the tax amount, since millage can change. Newly added property, property with 2024 construction, and property with a 2024 Assessable Transfer of Interest may be uncapped or only partly capped.

  • Appeals must be in writing with an original signature, sent to the Assessor.
  • The objection deadline is 90 days after notices are mailed, and the printed deadline on the 2025 notices was November 18, 2025.
  • If no notice was sent that year, the appeal period generally closes on the tax due date, typically January 15.
  • Later stages have 30-day deadlines, and filing an appeal does not delay the bill.

The Assessor's office is at 4050 Bridge View Dr., Suite 100, North Charleston, SC 29405, phone (843) 958-4100.

sections.h2: What is the 4% legal residence rate and what happens when the owner moves?
sections.html:
Owner-occupied homes are taxed at 4% of fair market value, other real property at 6%, and the 4% rate is not automatic. Under S.C. Code 12-43-220, the owner must have owned and occupied the home as a legal residence and be domiciled there.

Charleston County's Assessor says properties without approval are billed at 6%, and bills show "QR4" when the 4% rate applies. The application deadline is typically January 15. The statute also says the home may not be rented for more than 72 days in a calendar year, and an owner who loses eligibility must tell the assessor within six months or face a penalty of 100% of the tax paid plus interest.

That matters to sellers who moved out before listing. If the house has sat as a rental or vacant, the 6% rate can apply, and your payoff figure at closing will be higher than you expect.

sections.h2: What are the short-term rental rules in the city of Charleston?
sections.html:
The city sorts short-term rentals into categories, and each allows at most one STR unit per property. Category 1 is the Old and Historic District, Category 2 is the rest of the peninsula, and Category 3 covers Daniel Island, James Island, Johns Island and West Ashley.

  • Each category needs one extra off-street parking space beyond the two the zoning ordinance requires per dwelling unit.
  • Category 1 needs a structure individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
  • Category 2 needs a building constructed at least 50 years ago.

For eligibility, the city points owners to its property eligibility quiz or shorttermrental@charleston-sc.gov (city category page). A seller who is advertising a house as an investment with STR income should confirm the permit status in writing, since the permit rules depend on location.

sections.h2: What does selling a house with tax due look like in Charleston?
sections.html:
A seller who owes Charleston property tax can sell, and the unpaid amount is normally settled from the sale proceeds at closing. Request a payoff figure from the Treasurer's Office before you sign, since penalties step up on February 1 and March 17.

The Assessor's page confirms that refunds for overpaid taxes may be requested for up to two years, which can help a seller who paid at 6% while eligible for 4%. If you refinanced, the Treasurer reminds owners to send the bill to the mortgage holder so escrow pays it.

faqs.q: When is Charleston County property tax due?
faqs.a: January 15 of the following year is the last day without penalty, per the Charleston County Treasurer. A 3% penalty applies after that date, then a further 7% after February 1 and 5% after March 17.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Charleston assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days after the notice is mailed to send a written objection to the Assessor, with an original signature. The 2025 notices printed November 18, 2025 as the deadline. Phone, email and fax do not preserve your rights.

faqs.q: Is Charleston in more than one county?
faqs.a: Yes. The city spans Charleston and Berkeley counties, according to Wikipedia. Which county office you deal with depends on where the parcel sits, so check your tax bill before calling.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Charleston house if I owe back property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, and the unpaid tax is typically paid from the proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure first, because the 10% and 15% penalty totals begin after February 1 and March 17.

faqs.q: Does Charleston have a flood-zone disclosure tool?
faqs.a: The city issues a Flood Hazard Information Letter showing a property's flood zone. Requests for elevation certificates and flood hazard information go to floodplain-info@charleston-sc.gov.
